subject.title: fix(opencode): public models work without API keys

question: Should OpenClaw support anonymous OpenCode Zen inference for a provider-maintained set of temporary public models despite OpenCode’s published API-key requirement?
rationale: The patch is an intentional provider-auth policy change, not a mechanical correction: live behavior demonstrates current acceptance, while the provider’s documented contract and model eligibility source do not support the new guarantee.

options.title: Hold the current no-auth exception
options.body: Do not merge the hard-coded bypass unless OpenCode publishes or otherwise confirms a durable anonymous-inference contract.

options.title: Adopt an explicit experimental contract
options.body: Accept anonymous Zen access as an OpenClaw-supported mode, then define ownership, eligibility updates, user messaging, and failure behavior before merging.

options.title: Request provider-backed metadata
options.body: Ask for a documented endpoint or supported catalog signal that identifies anonymous models, then implement against that contract instead of a static list.

recommendation.title: Hold the current no-auth exception
recommendation.body: Do not merge the hard-coded bypass unless OpenCode publishes or otherwise confirms a durable anonymous-inference contract.

likelyOwner.reason: This contributor owns the current proposed implementation and has already documented the unresolved provider-contract boundary; current-main ownership evidence was unavailable.
